THE IDEA BEHIND ÉLAN

EST. 2026 / MADE FOR YOUNG MINDS

An idea worth
bringing to life.

It began with a conversation on the way back from lunch.
It became two days of ideas, decisions and new friendships.

Why we built Élan ↓
É

01 / WHERE IT BEGAN

It started
with a conversation.

Walking back from lunch, Akshit Parmar and Jacinth Jebaraj began talking about an idea. That conversation became the starting point for Élan, founded by Akshit with co-founders Sakshi Baldawa, Prachi Belagali and Jacinth.

The first Élan Summit took place at SGIS Pune Campus, Mulshi, on 5–6 September 2026. Across two days, the committee rooms and stage became the setting for our first chapter.

See the first edition ↗

02 / THE PURPOSE

A place to lead.
A reason to
take part.

We wanted students to have a part in the event, not just a seat in the audience.

At the first Élan Summit, students formed cabinets, worked through business challenges and presented decisions they had made together. The sessions gave them a reason to speak up and listen to people from other schools.

Outside the committee rooms, there were performances, conversations and a DJ night. Those shared moments were part of what we wanted Élan to be.

OUR MISSION

Make leadership, creativity and collaboration something young people can practise together.

03 / THE ORIGINAL FLAGSHIPS

Different rooms.
The same need to think.

01 / LEADERSHIP

Crisis
Command.

A nation in crisis. A cabinet under pressure. Work with your team, weigh the consequences and defend a response.

Inside the decision room ↗02 / ENTERPRISE

Cent$ible.

Build a brand or navigate a market. Bring strategy, creativity and judgement to a business arena that keeps changing.

Inside the idea room ↗

In the 2026 edition, the two flagships ran in parallel. For the second edition, Crisis Command will be the sole flagship. Cent$ible remains part of our first-edition story.

04 / WHAT MAKES IT ÉLAN

More than
the competition.

What happens between the sessions matters too.

01

Room to express yourself.

A stage for performance, a platform for ideas and the confidence to put something of your own into the world.

02

Responsibility you can feel.

From cabinet decisions to organising and volunteering, students take ownership of work that affects other people.

03

Connections beyond your school.

Mixed-school teams, shared activities and conversations give people a reason to meet and work together.

04

Care in the details.

The way people are welcomed, the spaces they share and the time between sessions all shape what they remember.
